Where it began

Shoaib Akhtar was born on 13 August 1975 in Morgah, a small town in Rawalpindi. He was the fourth of four brothers, with a younger sister after him, and it was his mother who chose his name.

He was a good student and had a place at Asghar Mall College, but cricket pulled harder. When trials for the PIA side were held in Lahore, he was so set on getting there that he rode on the roof of the bus. He caught the eye of Majid Khan, and after a good tour of England with Pakistan A in 1996 the Test call followed.

The player

His first Test came against the West Indies in 1997, on his home ground in Rawalpindi. The early wickets came slowly, but in 1999 everything clicked. In a Test at Calcutta he took eight wickets, and with consecutive balls he bowled Rahul Dravid and then Sachin Tendulkar. It was the first ball he had ever sent down to Tendulkar.

In 2005 he was the leading wicket-taker in a home series against England, with seventeen wickets. His slower ball, the last thing anyone expected from a man of his pace, proved too much for England's batters. Across 46 Tests from 1997 to 2007 he took 178 wickets at 25.69, with twelve five-wicket hauls, two ten-wicket matches and a best of six for 11.

What made him special

Speed, pure and simple. His 161.3 km/h was the fastest ball anyone had been timed at since speed guns came into international cricket in 1998. At the 2003 World Cup, against England, he sent down a ball measured at 100.2 miles an hour, making him one of only three bowlers ever to break the 100 mph barrier. Batters facing him had very little time to think, which was rather the idea.

With the bat he was a cheerful visitor rather than a resident. He made 544 Test runs at 10.26, and his best was 47. Three more and he would have had a fifty to frame, though he probably preferred the wickets anyway.

Away from the middle

In his first Indian Premier League match, for Kolkata Knight Riders in 2008, he defended a modest total of 133 against Delhi by taking four top-order wickets for 11 runs in three overs, and was named player of the match.

After cricket he became a familiar voice. He co-hosted a game show with Wasim Akram in 2017 and later started his own YouTube channel, where he talks cricket with fans and guests. By August 2023 it had about 3.73 million subscribers.

And finally

Long before he was the fastest bowler in the world, he travelled to his big trial on top of a bus. It seems fitting that a man who spent his career making things go quickly began it with the wind in his hair.
